chunks: Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from his father, who attributed it [to a higher authority], and said:

Mūsā ibn ʿImrān (peace be upon him) saw a man under the shade of the Throne and said, 'O Lord, who is this person whom You have brought so close that You have placed him under the shade of Your Throne?' Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, said, 'O Mūsā, this person was never undutiful to his parents, nor did he envy the people for what Allah had given them of His favors.' He asked, 'O Lord, are there any among Your creation who are undutiful to their parents?' He replied, 'The undutiful ones are not [counted as] theirs.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of 'uqūq' (undutifulness to parents) in determining a person's rank under the Divine Throne?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Moses (peace be upon him) observes a man beneath the Divine Throne, prompting Allah to attribute his elevated status to two key virtues: avoiding *'uqūq* (grave disobedience) to parents and refraining from envy (*hasad*) toward others' blessings. The divine clarification that the undutiful are not 'theirs' underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual continuity and merit derived from filial piety, distinguishing those who maintain strong familial bonds from those who sever them.
